question: Family planning was introduced in the __________ five - year plan.
solution:
The correct answer is __**first**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Family planning in India was first introduced during the First Five-Year Plan period (1951-1956).
 
• The program aimed to control the population growth rate and improve the health and well-being of families.
 
• It was the first organized and systematic approach towards population control in India.
 
• The initiative included measures such as promoting contraceptives, sterilization, and educating the public about family planning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)**

 
 
• India's First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, focusing on the agriculture sector, including irrigation and energy production.
 
• It was based on the Harrod-Domar model and aimed to address the immediate challenges of food shortage and inflation.
 
• The plan aimed to increase the national income by 11% over the five years and to achieve full employment.
 
• The government allocated significant resources to health and family planning to improve the overall well-being of the population.
 
 
 
• **Family Planning**
 
 
• Family planning is the practice of controlling the number of children in a family and the intervals between their births.
 
• It is achieved through the use of contraceptive methods and the treatment of involuntary infertility.
 
• Family planning is a key component of reproductive health and aims to ensure that individuals have the knowledge and means to decide freely and responsibly the number and spacing of their children.
 
• Effective family planning can help reduce maternal and infant mortality, improve women's health, and contribute to economic development.
 
 
 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**
 
 
• Five-Year Plans are centralized and integrated national economic programs developed by the Planning Commission of India.
 
• The plans were designed to achieve specific economic goals over five years, focusing on different sectors such as agriculture, industry, and infrastructure.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, and subsequent plans were developed to address emerging economic challenges and priorities.
 
• Although the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015, the legacy of the Five-Year Plans continues to influence India's economic planning and policy-making.
